candidate_name: Côte d'Ivoire–Benin–Togo joint LNG import framework (pooled FSRU, site TBD)
sponsor_or_proposer: Governments of Côte d'Ivoire, Benin and Togo; World Bank Group (backer). No private sponsor/operator named.
current_state: Regional pooled-LNG-import framework agreed at an energy-ministers meeting in Abidjan on 2025-12-07. Final declaration sets three priorities: pool LNG imports across the three countries, stand up a technical working group within one month to design an operating model, and develop a bankable project structure with World Bank assistance. No host country chosen for any FSRU/terminal, no site, no capacity, no sponsor/operator, no MOU/FEED/tender. Côte d'Ivoire's Baleine field is the only named existing gas infrastructure; a separate CIV–Ghana bidirectional pipeline is in exploratory phase.
missing_threshold_elements: Sponsor (only the World Bank as backer; no developer/operator for a Benin terminal); approximate location within Benin (regional pooled-import concept, no host country or port selected — an FSRU could land in CIV or Togo instead); concrete step (working-group-to-be-formed and a non-binding declaration only — no MOU/site selection/FEED/permit).
watch_for: Technical working group output / operating-model design; selection of a host country and port for any shared FSRU (whether Benin is the siting choice); a named developer or FSRU operator; an MOU, FEED award, or tender; any World Bank/IFC/MIGA project structure or financing reaching board. If a Benin-sited terminal with a sponsor + port emerges, promote to new_terminals. Re-check ~2026-12.
notes: Corroborated by two independent outlets: Ecofin Agency (2025-12-09) and Togo First (https://www.togofirst.com/en/energy/0812-17753-cote-d-ivoire-benin-togo-agree-on-regional-gas-coordination-mechanism, 2025-12-08). Both URLs PASS url_verifier (tokens: Benin, gas[, LNG]).
